title: Roja rambutan (NSIC Rm 06): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Roja rambutan: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Roja rambutan is a rambutan variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Roja is a registered rambutan variety, also sold or known as NSIC Rm 06. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2003 as NSIC 2003 Rm 06. Mario Tenorio bred it. Its record notes a yield of 70 to 80 kg.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Roja rambutan is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Rm 06, this is the same rambutan. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [rambutan variety finder](/crop-varieties/rambutan), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: **Yield:** a recorded yield of 70 to 80 kg.

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Roja was about 15 years old and about 25 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 70 to 80 kg. It bears every year, with fruit in July September. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit rambutan fields most often: [cacao pod borer](/pests/cacao-pod-borer), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Roja weighs about 45.85 grams, and its shape is oblong. The flesh is white and smooth. Its sweetness measured 20.88 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 55.94 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as July September, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Oblong, about 46 g, red skin, smooth, juicy white flesh, about 21 Brix, about 56 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a big fruited red Laguna rambutan, Roja is one of the five rambutan groups in Philippine studies. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Roja rambutan

Pick a registered selection whose flesh comes off the seed cleanly, which buyers pay more for. Plant budded trees. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Rm 06 the same as Roja?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Rm 06 is another name for Roja, registered as NSIC 2003 Rm 06. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 70 to 80 kg. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Roja?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
